chapter: Caravan, Perdido and the first tunes
title: Duke arranged every tune; naming Caravan and Conga Brava
summary: Duke arranged and recorded everything Tizol wrote; he left titles to Duke or Mills and wrote Conga Brava on request during the conga craze.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Uh huh. Did you arrange it, or did Duke arrange it?

Everything that I did, Duke arranged. All my tunes. I got quite a few tunes; I don't know if you know them all by their names, but I did quite a few tunes. I don't get too much -- a dollar, three dollars, four dollars, ten dollars -- but I get some all the time. Like Meditation, "Lost in Meditation," "Bakiff," "Conga Brava," "Pyramid," "Gypsy Without A Song, "Admiration" -- also a lot of things that I did that Duke recorded for me; that's the way I got the money, because he always recorded. And on every one of those tunes, I was always playing a little solo somewhere on that particular tune.
Did you do the titles of the songs?
No, I left that to Duke or to Irving Mills.
I don't know, unless Irving Mills did. Irving Mills says he wrote the lyrics, I don't know if that's true or not.
Juan, you named some of your tunes, "Conga Brava," because you named Congo-Rock, a few Spanish tunes.
Well, I wrote this particular thing. At that time, when they were playing a lot of congas, he asked me to write something like that, so I wrote it, and I called it "Conga Brava." Congo-Rock.
